external_invariants: Model is ResNetForImageClassification loaded from the local assets directory only (local_files_only=True) in float32; no downloads.
All weights and activations remain FP32; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 and torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 are False and torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest').
Seed policy: torch.manual_seed(20261020) applied in prepare, matching common.configure().

Input is the real preprocessed image fixture tensor from assets/pixels.npy (3 images, NCHW float32), selected as images[torch.arange(batch) % len(images)].contiguous(); for the frozen 'online' workload batch=1, i.e. the first image, unchanged every repeat.
The model is in eval() mode and the forward pass runs under torch.inference_mode(), identical to the source infer() helper calling model(pixel_values=pixels).logits.
Batch size is fixed at 1 for this workload; the workload, data, precision and output requirements are not altered to improve the score.
Correctness requires all logits within atol=1e-4 / rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 argmax equality against the reference; observations include every logit and the predicted class integer.

Latency is wall time around run() with CUDA synchronization at both boundaries, per the source's per-repeat timing; throughput is derived from the unchanged work amount (batch=1) and the measured elapsed time.
The adapter does not initialize CUDA or load the model at import time and never destroys the process group in reset.

selection.rationale: Single-device batch=1 FP32 ResNet-18 inference; communication is not applicable, so the only lever for latency_ms is the serialized GPU critical path plus dispatch overhead. This leaf aten::conv2d group is the single largest kernel-time owner in the frozen workload: 203.0 diagnostic CUDA us of the 727.7 us project total (~28%), ahead of the next leaf group (115.5 us). It contains exactly the three stage-4 convolutions with input [1,512,7,7], weight [512,512,3,3], padding 1, stride 1 (calls 417724ae..., c74ed565..., f9b932ed..., ~67.7 us each). Per-call kernel evidence shows cuDNN's deterministic heuristic (cudnn.benchmark is fixed False by the source policy) picked a Winograd pair: generateWinogradTilesKernel ~11.4 us plus _5x_cudnn_ampere_scudnn_winograd_128x128_ldg1_ldg4_relu_tile148n_nt_v1 ~56.1 us launched with grid [16,1,1] x 256 threads, i.e. only 16 CTAs, a severe under-occupancy on this Ampere-class GPU, with ~17% of each call spent purely in the input transform. The identical-FLOP control inside the same forward pass (the three 256x256x3x3 convs at 14x14, group 7fb0d2de3e359d451ab3, also ~231 MFLOPs each) runs in ~34 us per call, proving ~2x better throughput is reachable for this FLOP count on this device; the 7x7/512-channel shape is simply mis-served by the fixed heuristic. All three calls share one shape and one dispatch site (ResNetConvLayer Conv2d in the last stage), so a single coherent edit to the project's forward path for this exact shape (for example a shape-specific alternative FP32 implementation such as im2col+GEMM or a different conv algorithm selection that keeps TF32 disabled and numerics within atol/rtol 1e-4 with exact top-1) covers every call in the group with no co-dependent edits elsewhere. Coverage is complete (81/81 kernels associated), so no hidden cost is being traded away. Caveats kept in view: durations are diagnostic and inclusive; the clean baseline is 1.6307 ms wall per repeat while total GPU busy time is only ~0.73 ms, so the workload is partly CPU-dispatch bound and kernel-time savings may not translate one-to-one into latency_ms; the expected benefit is a hypothesis to be tested by the framework's measurement, not a claim.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing the Winograd path used for the three [1,512,7,7]x[512,512,3,3] stride-1 convolutions with a better FP32 implementation for this exact shape (while keeping cudnn.benchmark False, TF32 disabled, and logits within 1e-4 tolerance with exact top-1) will roughly halve their per-call cost from ~67.7 us toward the ~34 us already achieved by the equal-FLOP 256ch/14x14 convolutions, removing on the order of 90-110 us from the serialized GPU critical path (~12-15% of the 727.7 us diagnostic total). Because the measured wall latency (1.6307 ms) exceeds GPU busy time, the realized latency_ms improvement may be smaller than the kernel-time saving, and correctness must be revalidated; if the alternative algorithm's summation order breaks the 1e-4 logit tolerance, the fallback is a different algorithm choice within cuDNN for this shape rather than a math rewrite. The proposal is accepted or rejected on the independently measured latency_ms and quality evidence, not on this prediction.

proposal.rationale: Selected leaf group 5621410346ca09a421d0 is the three stage-4 aten::conv2d calls with input [1,512,7,7] (stride (25088,49,7,1)) and weight [512,512,3,3] (stride (4608,9,3,1)), stride=[1,1], padding=[1,1], dilation=[1,1], groups=1, bias=None. Diagnostic evidence (target-resources.json) shows cuDNN's fixed heuristic (cudnn.benchmark is frozen False) serves each of them with a Winograd pair totalling ~67.4-67.9 us, the main tile kernel launching only grid [16,1,1] x 256 threads (16 CTAs) with ~11.4 us spent in the input-transform kernel alone, while the equal-FLOP 256ch/14x14 convolutions elsewhere in the same forward reach ~34 us. The replacement re-expresses exactly these convolutions as aten::im2col (which performs the zero padding inside the im2col kernel, one launch) followed by one FP32 cuBLAS GEMM via torch.matmul(weight.view(512,4608), columns) -> [1,512,49] -> view(1,512,7,7). The im2col column ordering (c-major, then 3x3 kernel index) matches weight.view(512,4608) exactly, verified numerically on CPU against F.conv2d (max relative deviation ~2e-6 with unit-normal random weights, i.e. ordinary FP32 summation-reordering noise). The GEMM is 512x49x4608 (~231 MFLOP) and runs under the frozen policies untouched: torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 stays False (so cuBLAS uses true FP32 SGEMM), cudnn flags and cudnn.benchmark=False are not modified, no global torch state is changed, and the equal-FLOP control convolutions demonstrate ~2x better throughput for this FLOP count on this device. Each replacement carries a strict signature guard (exact observed shape/stride/dtype/device, bias None, stride/padding/dilation [1,1], groups 1); any other signature falls back to the parent reference callable with the original arguments, so semantics are preserved for unobserved signatures and the framework's phase/signature composition stays valid. No module.forward wrapper is installed and no fixture-dependent output is cached; every invocation executes the workload. Expected effect is ~30-35 us GPU time saved per call (~90-105 us of the 727.7 us diagnostic total); because measured wall latency (1.6307 ms) exceeds total GPU busy time, the realized latency_ms gain may be smaller - the path adds two extra CPU dispatches per call (im2col, matmul, plus views) while removing the Winograd transform launch, keeping kernel count roughly neutral. This is the first attempt; inputs/previous-feedback.txt does not exist, so there is no prior feedback to incorporate. Accept or reject on the framework's independently measured latency_ms and quality evidence.

setup_work.description: build() resolves the im2col entry point with one tiny CPU probe tensor (falls back to torch.nn.functional.unfold if aten::im2col is unavailable), binds torch.matmul and the per-call parent reference into three closures, and returns the mapping. No CUDA work, no kernel launches, no weight pre-packing, no parameter mutation, no persistent buffers, no CUDA Graph capture, and no global torch/backend flag changes at build or run time. The [512,4608] weight operand is a zero-copy view created per call from the guarded contiguous weight.
setup_work.setup_allocations: None on GPU at build time (CPU probe tensor of 4 floats only).
setup_work.per_run_transients: Per replaced call the fast path transiently allocates the im2col columns [1,4608,49] (~0.90 MiB FP32) and the GEMM output [1,512,49] (~0.10 MiB); both are freed to the caching allocator immediately after the call and no pools are retained, so framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes/framework.lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes should see no new retained memory and framework.peak_allocated_bytes (reset per run) may rise by at most ~0.9 MiB transiently. This is a per-call transient buffer, not a physical-memory saving claim.

quality_risks: Summation order differs from the reference cuDNN Winograd kernels (both are FP32); the conv outputs and therefore the final logits will deviate slightly. CPU sanity comparison against F.conv2d with unit-normal random weights showed max relative deviation ~2e-6 at the conv output (max abs ~1.1e-4 on activations of magnitude ~68-260 with random N(0,1) weights, which are ~10x larger than trained ResNet weights), comfortably inside the atol=rtol=1e-4 logit tolerance, but final acceptance depends on the framework's paired quality measurement.

exact_top1 could flip only if the top-2 logits were separated by less than the induced perturbation (~1e-5 or smaller); the argmax gaps of the reference logits are expected to be far larger, and if the check fails the framework restores the parent implementation.

The replacement adds two CPU-side aten dispatches per call in a workload whose wall latency (1.6307 ms) already exceeds GPU busy time (~0.73 ms), so the dispatch-bound regime may absorb part of the ~90-105 us GPU-time saving; the latency_ms outcome is decided by the framework's measurement, not by the kernel-time arithmetic.

Any signature not matching the observed one (different shape, stride, dtype, device, bias, stride/padding/dilation, groups) silently falls back to the parent aten::conv2d reference, so unexpected shapes incur the original cost and semantics rather than failure.
